patterns.content: Error handling: always check errors explicitly. if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf('context: %w', err) }. Use %w to wrap for errors.Is/errors.As.
defer for cleanup: defer file.Close() immediately after opening a file — runs on function exit regardless of path taken.
Goroutines + channels for concurrency. go func() { ch <- result }(). Use sync.WaitGroup for fan-out. Prefer channels over shared memory.
Interfaces are implicit — no implements keyword. Small interfaces preferred (io.Reader has 1 method). Accept interfaces, return structs.
Named return values for documentation, not logic: func divide(a, b float64) (result float64, err error). Naked return only in very short functions.
Use slices over arrays. append(slice, elem) returns a new slice — assign the result. Preallocate with make([]T, 0, capacity) when size is known.
struct embedding for composition: type Logger struct { io.Writer; prefix string } — Logger inherits Writer methods. No inheritance hierarchy.
context.Context as first parameter for cancellation/deadlines: func Fetch(ctx context.Context, url string) error. Never store context in a struct.
Table-driven tests: tests := []struct{ input string; want int }{ {'a', 1}, {'b', 2} }; for _, tt := range tests { t.Run(tt.input, func...) }
Zero value is useful: var m map[string]int is nil but safe to read from; var s []int is nil but len/cap return 0. Initialize only when you need to write.
